clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old man with well-controlled HIV on ART (CD4 542/μL) and a 30-year history of psoriasis presented with recurrent generalized scaly erythema requiring hospitalization. During admission, routine syphilis screening revealed positive TPPA with high-titer positive TRUST (1:2048). Skin biopsy was performed to differentiate from psoriasis flare, demonstrating histopathological features consistent with syphilis including plasma cell infiltration of the superficial dermis and perivascular areas with superficial vascular hyperplasia. The patient was treated with benzathine penicillin 2.4 million units intramuscularly weekly for 3 weeks, resulting in significant clinical improvement with diminution of the lesions, confirming the diagnosis of psoriasiform secondary syphilis masquerading as psoriasis.
